description: The Archivists is a team of two. One to build the technology, the other to preserve a story
summary: We developed an interactive storytelling web game that requires zero download, available on school computers and PCs for students aged 9-18 to learn about abandoned machinery in outer space through dialogue and exploration. The style is similar to old retro computer games, giving it that cozy, nostalgic feel. The reason is simple: many children are unaware that NASA data exists online for anyone to read, and so they never get to experience any of the research that has been conducted in space. Our project aims to bring that information to students in a simple and fun way, encouraging them to learn and research through a pixelated, fast-paced storytelling game.
details:
Our project consists of a web hosted, retro-style, exploration and storytelling game that provides children aged 9-18 with baseline information about previous NASA missions conducted on Mars and the Moon, including but not limited to rover history, ground composition, gravity and technology. Players start in the Hub, an orbital NASA archive. From there, they can visit the Moon and its LRV, as well as Mars and its Sojourner Rover. They collect blueprints containing hardware information, interact with the rover and unlock stories, and all the uncovered data gets sent back to the computer in the Hub. Users can even go back and review the notes, and download them as a txt file. Currently, only the Moon and Mars are available as locations, but we plan on expanding to Solar Orbit, Deep Space, and other Moons. The project aims to create a thirst for knowledge in children, and encourage learning. The graphics were done by hand on Pixsquare by the team’s graphic designer, and the story was brainstormed by both team members, because human-to-human transmission of ideas works best, especially for younger ages. HTML5 and JavaScript were both used to code the game, which can be run on any computer, as well as a mobile version. Project Abandoned but not Forgotten: The Last Transmission is original because it tackles the empathic side of children, letting them sympathize with the rovers and their stories, adding emotional depth to an educational game.
To make the game accessible to all, all the dialogues are captioned and saved in the game’s log, available to be reviewed by the user. Players aged 8-12 play as Explorers, collecting blueprints and interacting with rovers. Players aged 13-18 play as Archivists, which is the same gameplay but with added data and information that would be more valuable to older kids. With or without sound, the game is equally immersive, and can be enjoyed even in quiet environments. Additionally, we plan on expanding the game to include more locations and data, RAG AI models for each rover to add dynamics, as well as different languages to select from, since we hope children worldwide will want to play it and learn.

Link to the project's GitHub repository: https://github.com/WJ812/abandoned-but-not-forgotten-the-last-transmission
